nodes.summary: For a list $L$ of blocked names, the test returns true on a label exactly when the label is the silent action $\tau$, or an input or an output on a name that does not occur in $L$. It is the Boolean form of the condition that restriction by $L$ allows the label.
nodes.title: Boolean restriction test

nodes.summary: Let $s$ list the labelled transitions $(a, x')$ of each implementation code $x$, let $t$ list those of each specification code $y$, and let $R$ be a finite list of code pairs. The backward check succeeds when for every pair $(x, y)$ in $R$ and every entry $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$, at least one of the following holds: $a = \tau$ and $(x, y')$ is in $R$; some entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$ with the same label has $(x', y')$ in…
nodes.title: Backward certificate check

nodes.summary: For transition lists $s$ of implementation codes and $t$ of specification codes and a finite list $R$ of code pairs, the certificate check succeeds when both the forward check and the backward check succeed on $s$, $t$ and $R$.
nodes.title: Weak-bisimulation certificate check

nodes.summary: Fix a recursive specification, a map $\iota$ from codes to process constants and a function $s$ listing labelled transitions for each code. Suppose that for every code $x$, writing $(a_1, y_1), \dots, (a_n, y_n)$ for the entries of $s(x)$ in order, the body of the constant $\iota(x)$ is $a_1.\iota(y_1) + (a_2.\iota(y_2) + \dots + (a_n.\iota(y_n) + 0))$, which is $0$ when $n = 0$. Then the processes $\iota(x)$,…
nodes.title: Constants listing their transitions realize them

nodes.summary: Let $s$ list the labelled transitions $(a, x')$ of each implementation code $x$, let $t$ list those of each specification code $y$, and let $R$ be a finite list of code pairs. The forward check succeeds when for every pair $(x, y)$ in $R$ and every entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$, either $a = \tau$ and $(x', y)$ is in $R$, or some entry $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$ with the same label has $(x', y')$ in $R$.
nodes.title: Forward certificate check

nodes.summary: Given functions $s$ and $t$ listing the labelled transitions of codes $x$ and $y$, the transitions of the pair $(x, y)$ are listed in three blocks: $(a, (x', y))$ for each entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$; then $(a, (x, y'))$ for each entry $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$; then $(\tau, (x', y'))$ for each entry $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$ and each entry $(b, y')$ of $t(y)$ whose labels are complementary, that is, one is the input and the…
nodes.title: Code-level parallel composition

nodes.summary: Fix a recursive specification. If the processes $P_x$ realize $s$ and the processes $Q_y$ realize $t$, then the parallel compositions $P_x \mid Q_y$, indexed by pairs $(x, y)$, realize the code-level parallel composition of $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Parallel composition preserves realization

nodes.summary: Fix a recursive specification. A family of processes $P_x$ indexed by codes $x$ realizes a function $s$ that lists, for each code $x$, labelled transitions $(a, y)$ with $a$ a label and $y$ a code, when for every code $x$, every label $a$ and every process $q$, the process $P_x$ has a transition with label $a$ to $q$ exactly when $s(x)$ contains an entry $(a, y)$ with $P_y = q$.
nodes.title: Realization of a code-level transition system

nodes.summary: For a list $L$ of blocked names and a function $s$ listing the labelled transitions of each code, the restricted transitions of a code $x$ are the entries $(a, y)$ of $s(x)$, in order, whose label $a$ is the silent action $\tau$ or an input or an output on a name that does not occur in $L$.
nodes.title: Code-level restriction

nodes.summary: Fix a recursive specification and a list $L$ of blocked names. If the processes $P_x$ realize $s$, then the restricted processes $P_x \setminus L$ realize the code-level restriction of $s$ by $L$.
nodes.title: Restriction preserves realization

nodes.summary: Given code-level transition functions $s$ on codes $\alpha$ and $t$ on codes $\beta$, each listing labelled steps to codes, a relation $R$ given as a list of code pairs, and codes $x$ and $y$, the root check succeeds exactly when every listed step $(a, x')$ of $s(x)$ is matched by some listed step $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$ with the same label and $(x', y') \in R$, and every listed step $(a, y')$ of $t(y)$ is matched by…
nodes.title: Direct check of the root condition

nodes.summary: Let $f$ realize the code-level transition function $s$ and $g$ realize $t$ for a recursive specification, and let $R$ be a list of code pairs on which the certificate check of $s$, $t$ and $R$ succeeds. If the root check of $s$, $t$ and $R$ succeeds at codes $x$ and $y$, then the processes $f(x)$ and $g(y)$ are rooted weakly bisimilar (observation congruent) in the labelled transition system of the specification…
nodes.title: Certificate checks give rooted observation congruence

nodes.summary: For every recursive specification, every list $l$ of pairs of a label and a process, every label $a$ and every process $q$, the sum of the prefixes listed in $l$ has a transition labelled $a$ to $q$ exactly when $(a, q)$ belongs to $l$.
nodes.title: Transitions of a sum of prefixes

nodes.summary: For a list $l$ of pairs $(a, q)$ of a label and a process, the process that chooses among the prefixes $a.q$ listed in $l$: the empty list gives the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$, and the list with head $(a, q)$ and tail $r$ gives the choice $a.q + P$ between the prefix $a.q$ and the process $P$ built in the same way from $r$.
nodes.title: Sum of prefixes

nodes.summary: Let $f$ realize the code-level transition function $s$ and $g$ realize $t$ for a recursive specification, and let $R$ be a list of code pairs on which the certificate check of $s$, $t$ and $R$ succeeds. Then for every pair $(x, y)$ in $R$, the processes $f(x)$ and $g(y)$ are weakly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of the specification.
nodes.title: Certificate checks give weak bisimilarity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
